🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a joint news conference with Secretary General of the CSTO Taalatbek Masadykov
(Moscow, November 10, 2026)
Key points
:
•
As #CSTO Chair in 2026
,
Russia has pursued a policy of steadily deepening integration across all areas
to improve the Organisation’s effectiveness and enhance its international standing.
We are grateful to our allies
for their consistent support for all our initiatives throughout Russia’s chairmanship.
• We were also compelled to discuss
Armenia’s failure to fulfil its obligations under
the CSTO Charter
regarding annual contributions to our common Organisation’s budget.
There can be no ambiguity here.
•
A draft decision
on this matter will also be considered at
tomorrow’s Session of the CSTO Collective Security Council
. It provides for
suspending Armenia’s right to nominate its citizens
for quota-based positions in the Organisation’s bodies and
withdrawing its voting rights until its arrears are paid in full
.
• At the proposal of the American mediators,
the talks that began today in Abu Dhabi
focus on
discussing the parameters of a future security architecture for Ukraine, Russia and our entire region
–
European security
, one might say.
•
Ursula von der Leyen
said
there should be no discussion of the parameters of a security architecture until a lasting truce is in place.
The same old logic again
: they must “buy time” for their “clients” – the Kiev regime – and use it to replenish Ukraine’s military losses.
❌
We will not agree to this.
• As for European participation, they have flown to Abu Dhabi. Let them sit in their hotel.
But we cannot and do not wish to prevent the Americans from talking to whoever they deem necessary, on the grounds that this will help the negotiations
. We shall see what comes of it.
•
The idea of defining clear parameters for a future security architecture before moving on to settling the Russian-Ukrainian conflict itself is
entirely reasonable
.
• We have seen the Kiev regime’s ploys
time and again
.
❌
We will not agree to another truce, ceasefire or whatever it may be called without understanding the next steps.
• Europe’s plan is very simple, and they make no secret of it.
As soon as a ceasefire is in place, they will deploy “stabilisation forces”
to territory controlled by the Kiev regime. Through this concept, which we will, of course, prevent them from implementing,
they seek to stabilise the current Nazi regime
.
• Regarding
the situation surrounding Iran
and US President
Donald Trump
’s statement that Washington is no longer considering military options,
I hope that will indeed be the case
. Russia and China have consistently stressed
the need to return to a peaceful settlement
through political and diplomatic means.
•
Unfortunately, external actors continue to play a destructive role
, as was the case with
the Islamabad Memorandum
, signed by Iran’s Leader and President Donald Trump personally. Despite this,
Israel refuses to comply with its first provision
, which stipulates the need for non-interference in the internal affairs of the Lebanese Republic.
• Prospects for a settlement in
the Strait of Hormuz
and, more broadly, around
the entire Arabian Peninsula
, as I would put it, will require
consideration of the situation in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
. We need to understand how to accommodate the Houthis’ legitimate interests in the context of the Yemeni crisis.

🗓
On November 10 in Moscow, Russia’s Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
chaired a joint meeting
of
the Council of Foreign Ministers, the Council of Defence Ministers and the Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation
(
#CSTO
).
Taalatbek Masadykov
, who took office as CSTO Secretary General on January 1, 2026, also took part.
The participants held a constructive and engaged exchange of views on
pressing international and regional issues
.
👉
Sergey Lavrov's remarks at the Plenary Session of the International Collective Security Forum
They discussed
the situation in the CSTO’s area of responsibility and neighbouring regions
and reaffirmed their commitment to working more closely together to strengthen the Organisation’s ability to counter growing security challenges and threats. These include
the rising risk of conflict, terrorist activity, drug trafficking, illegal migration and crimes involving information and communications technologies
.
✍️
The participants
reviewed a number of documents for subsequent approval by the CSTO Collective Security Council
. They endorsed
decisions to further strengthen the Organisation’s capabilities
, including measures to develop its Collective Aviation Forces and air defence capabilities and to ensure biological security in the CSTO’s area of responsibility. They also endorsed
several joint political statements
, including
the Summit’s final declaration
.
The participants paid particular attention to
strengthening interparliamentary cooperation
as the CSTO Parliamentary Assembly marks its 20th anniversary. They endorsed
the draft Agreement on the CSTO Parliamentary Assembly
.
A plan of events
was prepared for signature by the Heads of State to mark two anniversaries in 2027 –
35 years since the signing of the Collective Security Treaty
and
25 years since the establishment of the CSTO
.
The participants agreed to submit
documents on the staffing of the Organisation’s permanent bodies
to the Heads of State.
👉
Sergey Lavrov's remarks at the joint meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers, the Council of Defence Ministers and the Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils of the CSTO
Tajikistan’s Foreign Minister
Sirojiddin Muhriddin
briefed the participants on his country’s priorities for its CSTO chairmanship in 2027.
🤝
The next meeting of the CSTO Council of Foreign Ministers will take place
in Tajikistan in the first half of 2027
.

🎙
Remarks and response to a question
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the Plenary Session of
the International Collective Security Forum
(Moscow, November 10, 2026)
Key points
:
•
Russian initiatives to establish a single treaty-based legal framework for security across Europe were rejected
. I remember very clearly reminding our Western colleagues of the principle of indivisible security. It requires that no country or organisation in the Euro-Atlantic area strengthen its own security
at the expense of others
or lay claim to dominance.
•
As you know, our most recent attempt came in December 2021, when we tried to prevent
the inevitable
. I want to stress that point, as President
Vladimir Putin
has explained on more than one occasion. We knew for certain that serious preparations were under way, with Western support, for
a major military crackdown on Donbass
(the Donetsk and Lugansk People’s Republics).
We could not allow that to happen.
•
We have no illusions about the administration of US President
Donald Trump
. We recognise the fundamental differences between us over the future course of international politics.
☝️
Even so,
it is always better to talk
. That was true even during the Cold War, when our military maintained contact with their American counterparts. It remains true of our relations with the US today.
•
We have our own position paper [on a new security architecture in Eurasia]
. We also have what
#CSTO
Secretary General
Taalatbek Masadykov
has just outlined. The CSTO works closely with other subregional organisations on the continent, including the
#CIS
and the
#SCO
, and has signed memoranda of cooperation with them.
•
Africa
has around a dozen subregional organisations.
Latin America
, too, certainly has around ten such organisations. Both regions also have
a continent-wide umbrella organisation
that brings all their countries together.
Eurasia
, the world’s largest continent, rich in natural resources and densely populated,
has no such umbrella organisation
. Yet closer links are essential if we are to achieve a sensible division of labour and make the most of the advantages that God and history have bestowed on the peoples of Eurasia.
We need those links to avoid duplication and optimise logistics projects and transport routes.
•
Our aim is to come together and take stock of what we already have
– the subregional organisations already in place and the links between them.
We have no plans to create a new organisation
. Consider the links between
the EAEU and ASEAN, the SCO and ASEAN, the EAEU and the SCO, and those linking the CIS, the SCO and the CSTO. To some extent, what we call
the “integration of integrations”
is already under way.

🎙
Remarks
by Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the joint meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers, the Council of Defence Ministers and the Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils of
the Collective Security Treaty Organisation
(Moscow, November 10, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
We are pleased to welcome you to Moscow for this regular joint meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers, the Council of Defence Ministers and the Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils of
the Collective Security Treaty Organisation
(
#CSTO
).
As Russia chairs the Organisation in 2026, we attach particular importance to the success of today’s meeting
. Throughout our chairmanship, we have sought to make fuller use of the
#CSTO
’s potential for integration to deepen cooperation and partnership with our closest allies across all areas.
I am grateful to my fellow Ministers for the engaging Session we held earlier today at
the International Collective Security Forum
.
We had a frank and professional exchange of views
, which experts will take up in their discussions.
☝️
I am confident that
the Forum’s
work will contribute to building
a free, multipolar and democratic world order
.
👉
This entails building a new security architecture on our shared continent of Eurasia
, based on the principles of equal and indivisible security and open to all countries on the continent willing to engage constructively on an equal footing.
During Russia’s chairmanship, we have placed particular emphasis on
closer foreign policy coordination
, on
countering both traditional and new challenges and threats
, and on s
trengthening the CSTO’s military capabilities
.
We have worked hard to reinforce the CSTO’s role as a key guarantor of regional security.
This work reflects
the priorities
that Russia’s President
Vladimir Putin
, this year’s Chair of the Collective Security Council, set out with the support of the member states.
🤝
We are grateful to our friends for their steadfast support as we pursue the objectives of Russia’s chairmanship.
These efforts serve our common interests.

item.title: ✉️ Russia's President Vladimir Putin sent greetings to the participants, guests and organisers of
item.description: ✉️ Russia's President Vladimir Putin sent greetings to the participants, guests and organisers of the International Collective Security Forum (November 10, 2026) ✍️ I am pleased to welcome you to Moscow for the opening of the International Collective Security Forum , held as part of Russia’s chairmanship of the Collective Security Treaty Organisation ( #CSTO ). The Forum has brought together representatives of government bodies, defence ministries and the defence industry, as well as scientists and experts. During the plenary sessions and roundtable discussions, you will assess the impact of today’s challenges on the geopolitical situation in Eurasia and explore ways to strengthen regional security and stability . The CSTO Member States have gained considerable experience in working together constructively. At the same time, given the continuing international tensions, it is clear that we must further strengthen the Organisation’s capabilities and work more closely together to address the tasks before it. 👉 Our priorities include defence, countering terrorism and extremism, and combating cybercrime, drug trafficking and illegal migration. I am confident that the Forum will take place in a constructive atmosphere and that its proposals and initiatives will find practical application for the benefit of the peoples of our countries. 🤝 I wish you every success and all the very best. VLADIMIR PUTIN

item.content:encoded:

🗓
On November 9
, the international round table "
Militarization of Europe: What next?
" was held in Vienna, organized by the
Delegation of the Russian Federation to the Vienna Negotiations on Military Security and Arms Control
.
The event focused on analyzing
the current situation in Europe, marked by the unprecedented militarization
under the pretext of countering the "Russian threat".
#NATO
and the
#EU
are openly preparing for war against Russia
, predicting that it could break out within the next 3–5 years.
Participants discussed
the consequences of the massive increase in mil spending
by European countries, the
expansion of military infrastructure
in "frontline states" bordering Russia, and
NATO's provocative plans
against our country.
❗️
In 2025, military spending by NATO states already amounted to ~ $1.6 trln. In 2025, spending by the 27 EU states reached EUR 418 bln and is projected to rise to EUR 800 bln by 2030.
❗️
💊
Particular emphasis was placed on the
harmful effects of the intensive information and propaganda campaign
conducted by European countries to condition their own populations to accept the idea of an "inevitable" conflict with Russia.
The "Russian threat" is used to justify everything citizens are expected to sacrifice
in the struggle against our country. The increase in European military spending is taking place against a backdrop of
economic stagnation and will have serious social consequences.
💊
An important topic of discussion was the existing mechanisms for
de-escalation
, including those between Russia and NATO. It was noted that their use has become increasingly difficult, while bilateral de-escalation channels remain virtually frozen, including dialogue under
agreements on the prevention of incidents on and over the high seas, as well as on the prevention of dangerous military activities
.
💊
Special attention was paid to the Ukrainian crisis and its connection with European militarization.
Ukraine is being systematically integrated into the defense industries of European countries, while the battlefield experience of the Armed Forces of Ukraine is being used
to prepare for a conflict with our country.
The round table opened with a
video address by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation S.A. Ryabkov
. The event brought together representatives of the Vienna diplomatic corps, international and regional organizations, including the UN and the OSCE, as well as prominent experts and journalists.
🎙
Speakers at the round table included
:
- Head of a Division of the Department of International Military Cooperation of the MoD of the Republic of Belarus Lieutenant Colonel
E.Rusak
;
- Deputy Director of the Department for Non-Proliferation and Arms Control of the Russian MFA
A.Mazur
;
- Head of a Division of the 2nd CIS Department of the Russian MFA
A.Postigov
;
- Vice-Rector for International Relations and Security of the Russian State Academy of Intellectual Property, Reserve Colonel
A.Likhonosov
;
- Professor Emeritus of Political Science at Columbia University,
Dr. Robert Legvold
;
- Austrian political scientist and journalist
D.Reinisch
;
- Associate Professor at the Department of Political Philosophy and Geopolitics at Uni Dolomiti in Belluno, Italy,
L.M.Pacini
.
☝️
Following the round table,
we reiterate that Russia does not seek confrontation with NATO and does not want war with Europe
. European countries must abandon their dangerous course, which gives them the illusion of protection against external threats but will, in reality, lead to catastrophic consequences.
